newsitem.title: UK: LME reforms seen largely complete by year-end - SIB.
newsitem.headline: LME reforms seen largely complete by year-end - SIB.

text.p: Proposed changes to some practices at the London Metal Exchange (LME) should largely be completed by the end of the year, Jane Lowe, head of Derivatives Market Supervision at the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said.

"Most of the recommendations are expected to be implemented by the end of the year, although some issues, such as systems development, will take a little longer because of the complexity of the work involved," she said at the Financial Times World Aluminium Conference.
The SIB was asked by the LME to carry out a review of the exchange last June, following the announcement by Japan's Sumitomo Corp of losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
The SIB made its report last December, and the LME is currently implementing changes including warehousing, governance, and transparancy.
The SIB did not stipulate how change should be made - that was left to the LME - but it remains closely involved in monitoring the implementation process.

Lowe said that many of the issues on warehousing encompassed regulatory matters, as conflicts of interest could arise where warehouse companies are linked with firms involved with other aspects of metals in relation to inside information on stock holdings.
The SIB was asked by some to ban ownership of warehouse companies by metals trading groups.

"We did not accept this suggestion because our view is that it is the misuse of inside information which is wrong, not share ownership. However, it is clear that 'Chinese Walls' have to be maintained in these circumstances," she said.
